meta.disclaimer: Prototype built from public data. Figures carry their source, season and confidence. Not for trading decisions.
meta.intro: Where {commodity} are grown, what they are worth, who exports them and who runs the farms. Every figure carries its source and season; gaps are flagged, never hidden.

banana.name: Bananas
banana.scope_note: Fresh bananas; some national series include plantains
banana.season_basis: FAOSTAT calendar year. Australian figures for 2024/25 are mapped to 2024.

valuation_methods.label: Global price (US import)
valuation_methods.description: Every country's output valued at the World Bank US import price for that season.
valuation_methods.caveat: An import price at destination port. It includes shipping and overstates farm-gate value, most for domestic-market growers.

valuation_methods.label: Global price (EU import)
valuation_methods.description: Every country's output valued at the World Bank EU import price for that season.
valuation_methods.caveat: An import price at destination port; overstates farm-gate value.

valuation_methods.label: Local producer price
valuation_methods.description: Each country's output valued at its own farm-gate price, converted to USD.
valuation_methods.caveat: Most FAO producer prices in this sample are 2014-2018; where the price year differs from the season, the value is flagged.

AUS.note: About 500 farms, most family-run. The largest, the family-owned Mackay Farming Group, grows about 13% of national output across 9 farms.

ECU.note: About 5,000 small producers hold roughly 30% of plantations and sell through cooperatives to exporters; large, technically advanced growers supply most exports. Los Ríos, El Oro and Guayas held 91% of commercial area in 2009.

PHL.note: Export Cavendish comes from commercial plantations, from 2-20 ha monocrops up to multinational estates; smallholders mostly grow Saba and Lakatan for local markets. Mindanao held 99% of Cavendish in 2018.

ownership: Corporate for export, family for local

IND.note: State production is available. Farm counts by size and ownership need the Agriculture Census or Horticulture Statistics tables.

PHL.regions: PSA Major Fruit Crops regional tables

operators.name: Mindanao Banana Farmers and Exporters Association
Asociación de Exportadores de Banano del Ecuador (AEBE)

mango.name: Mangoes
mango.scope_note: Mangoes, mangosteens and guavas, as FAO and HS group them
mango.season_basis: FAOSTAT calendar year. Australian figures for 2020/21 are mapped to 2020.

valuation_methods.label: World export price
valuation_methods.description: Every country's output valued at the world average mango export price for that season.
valuation_methods.caveat: An export (FOB) price for traded fruit. It overstates the value of fruit sold on local markets, which is most mango output.

valuation_methods.label: Local producer price
valuation_methods.description: Each country's output valued at its own farm-gate price, converted to USD.
valuation_methods.caveat: No mango producer prices are in this sample yet.

AUS.note: The Northern Territory grew 54% of the 2020/21 crop and Queensland 43%. NT output reached 4.3 million trays in 2025-26 from about 6,350 ha, with Darwin and Katherine the two regions. Grower numbers are not in this sample.

IND.note: Uttar Pradesh and Andhra Pradesh grow about 40% of India's mangoes. Most fruit is sold fresh at home or processed into pulp; farm counts by size and ownership need the Agriculture Census.

PAK.regions: Pakistan Bureau of Statistics fruit tables

agent.name: Market Analyst
agent.analysis_prompt: You are the Market Analyst agent inside NavHub Markets, writing for a business user looking for market opportunities. Using ONLY the data in the JSON below (the figures currently on their screen), write a short analysis. Format: one bold headline sentence, then three short sections with '### ' headings: 'Where the volume and value are', 'Export opportunity', 'How far to trust this'. Use '- ' bullets, at most 3 per section, under 230 words in total. Quote figures as they appear in the data, with their season. Say when a figure is filled from an earlier season, derived, or rounded. Never invent numbers, countries or sources that are not in the data.
agent.chat_prompt: You are the Market Analyst agent inside NavHub Markets. The user is looking at the market view described in the JSON below and will ask questions about it. Answer from that data and from the page tools if you have them; if the data cannot answer, say what is missing and which source would fill it. Be direct and brief (under 150 words unless asked for more), use '- ' bullets for lists, quote figures with their season, and never invent numbers. If the user asks to see a different commodity, season, scope or map measure, use the change_view tool when available.
suggestions: Where is the biggest gap between production and exports?
Which exporters earn the most per tonne?
What would you check before trusting these numbers?
